title: Zen & the art of startup advice: why advice contradicts itself and how to filter it
summary: Dalton Caldwell argues that startup advice blogposts are self-contradictory when synthesized, much like the cold-reading "rainbow ruse." Succeeding means being comfortable holding contradictory information, distrusting black-and-white thinkers, and keeping emotions level in good times and bad.

principles.text: Startup advice, taken together, is deeply self-contradictory, so it is less useful than it feels.
principles.quote: if you tried to synthesize all of the available advice into a single coherent framework, you would quickly realize that the aggregate “advice framework” is deeply self-contradictory.

principles.text: Succeeding in startups and life requires being comfortable holding contradictory information.
principles.quote: nothing is black-and-white, and in fact, much of succeeding in life consists of being comfortable sitting with contradictory information

principles.text: Anxiety drives people to crave simple linear narratives and tidy formulas that explain success.
principles.quote: Anxious people eat this stuff up… anything to cure the squishy uncertainty in the pit of their stomachs.

principles.text: Keep your advice filter sharp: distrust black-and-white thinkers and oversimplified explanations of complex events.
principles.quote: Beware of black-and-white thinkers. Beware of people that present very simple narratives as the explanation of incredibly complex events. Don’t take anything you read too literally.

principles.text: Everyone feels uncertain; some just hide it better, so don't compare your insides to others' outsides.
principles.quote: Realize that _everyone_ feels this way, it’s just that some work harder than others to cover it up.

principles.text: Use a paired mantra to smooth emotional swings, since euphoria is as dangerous as despair.
principles.quote: Things are much worse than they seem, also, things are much better than they seem.
